messages.author: d194c7e3cac8dcfe
messages.subject: effort calculations
parts:
Hey everyone,
I'm hoping there is an easy fix to my problem, I thought I was almost done with my analysis!
I am trying to get monthly abundance estimates for right whales, so I have the month as my Region.label.  We have 16 tracklines (my Sample.Label) that we repeat every survey.  So, trackline 1 gets flown multiple times every month.  Because of this, I summed the effort for trackline 1 for April and this is what I put in the effort column for every sighting that was seen on trackline 1 in April (which now I'm realizing might be my problem?).  When I look at the results,  k = 16 which I think is correct since they are the same tracklines every time.  But, the effort seems to be a problem.  In April, for example, the results list the effort as the sum of the entire effort column from my flatfile.  In the minke data you provide as an example, it somehow knows to pull out the effort for trackline 1 only once for each region (instead of all the times it is listed for each sighting).  Unfortunately, I need the effort for trackline 1 more than once for each region, since we covered it more than once.  Is this possible?

Thank you!
~Laura Ganley

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] effort calculations
parts:
Laura

If I follow what you describe, I think you have set up your data properly.  You want the software to correctly recognise the number of spatial replicates you have (16 in your case), but you also want the encounter rate to be calculated correctly so the amount of distance flown is the length of a transect multiplied by the number of times it is flown in a month.  All seems proper.

What I don't understand is your assertion "I need the effort for trackline 1 more than once for each region".  I would not think this is the case; you collapse all sightings made in transect 1.  The idea of repeat flights lose their identity.
